methodology: Exceptions audit against the atlas country/territory directory. Unlisted places retain the standard default. Status describes statistical applicability, not travel advice or a sovereignty determination. A territory label never authorizes inheriting another jurisdiction's flows. A small population does not imply zero tourism or inherently prevent a 20-market table. Missing public rankings are not zero flows.

SH.note: This code combines St Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha. St Helena passenger series covers St Helena island, not all three. Government flags a change in immigration procedures and unavailable leisure/St Helenian classifications for 2025. Passenger totals include residents and are not tourist market rankings.

PN.note: Inhabited UK Overseas Territory; Pitcairn is the only inhabited island of the four. Its small population does not imply zero visitors or justify fabricated source markets. Use territory-specific tourism statistics, never UK flows.

sources.title: UN: Pitcairn working paper 2025
Government of the Pitcairn Islands

AQ.note: Antarctica has no permanent human resident population. Research personnel and expedition visitors are present; Antarctic tourism is substantial. A conventional resident outbound country ranking is not applicable. Expedition visitor nationality and landing statistics are separate measures.

sources.title: British Antarctic Survey: permanent inhabitants and staff
Antarctic Treaty Secretariat: tourism

BV.note: Bouvetøya is a protected Norwegian nature reserve. Landing or staying generally does not require a permit, but activities are strictly regulated, including seasonal protection of Nyrøysa. There is no ordinary visitor infrastructure. Do not substitute Norway-wide travel flows or interpret absent rankings as zero expedition visits.

sources.title: Norwegian Polar Institute: Bouvetøya nature reserve regulations

HM.note: Heard Island and McDonald Islands has no resident population. Scientific and occasional private expeditions are separate from an ordinary resident tourism economy; conventional resident outbound rankings are not applicable. Australian national travel flows must not be assigned here.

sources.title: Australian Antarctic Program: Heard Island
Australian Antarctic Program: Heard and McDonald Islands history

TF.note: The French Southern and Antarctic Lands has no permanent population. Scientific, technical and military personnel rotate through its districts. Expedition or vessel participation is not resident outbound tourism, and mainland France's country rankings cannot be inherited.

sources.title: TAAF administration: territory presentation

GS.note: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands has no permanent population; government and scientific staff are present. Cruise and yacht visitors travel by sea under territorial entry arrangements. Resident outbound rankings are not applicable; ship passenger statistics remain meaningful.

sources.title: Government of South Georgia: frequently asked questions
Government of South Georgia: how to visit

IO.note: The territorial administration states this is not a tourist destination and access requires permission. Outer-island yacht permits and access connected with Diego Garcia are distinct. Do not turn military or administrative movements into tourist arrivals or infer UK resident outbound flows.

sources.title: BIOT administration: visiting
BIOT administration: permits

UM.note: This is an aggregate of separate US islands and atolls, not one ordinary tourist destination. Access and staffing differ by island: Midway is closed to public visitation, while Palmyra has a small field-station workforce. Do not equate staff with a resident tourism market or inherit US travel flows.

SJ.note: This code combines Svalbard and Jan Mayen. Svalbard has resident communities and a tourism economy; Jan Mayen has rotating station personnel. Svalbard accommodation data must be labelled Svalbard rather than all SJ; do not assign Norway-wide travel markets.
